title: SilverLine pilot weekly token efficiency review
header: Date: 2025-11-12 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Recording: yes | Locale: en-US
summary: Weekly pilot sync focused on unit economics: tokens/sec/$, caching wins, and batching tradeoffs. Reviewed last week's benchmark (mixed chat + summarization), discussed KV/prefix cache hit patterns, looked at quantization impacts on throughput and quality, and agreed on a 24h production-shaped benchmark plus follow-up architecture deep-dive. Action items assigned for updated econ sheet, run longer runtime test with realistic session stickiness, and SSO/KMS checklist for next procurement milestone.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we've got about 50 minutes, quick agenda — recapped the telemetry, dig into tokens per dollar and then next steps. Uh Maya will run the perf notes.
[00:23] Maya (Redwood SE): Morning — so, quick summary: last 72-hour pilot run, mixed workload that mirrors SilverLine: 60% short chat, 30% multi-turn note summarization, 10% long form generation. Average seq len was 82 tokens for requests, response mean 140.
[00:40] Alex (SilverLine): Quick clar — when you say mixed, is that single-user sessions or batched many small ones? We saw a lot of stickiness per user.
[00:52] Maya: Good call. The run used sticky sessions with session affinity, so we preserved KV cache locality. That gave us higher effective cache hit rate than random routing.
[01:10] Priya (SilverLine SRE): We measured KV cache hit ~38% on the default config, prefix cache for frequent product names was closer to 62% when we pin by session.
[01:25] Maya: Right, that 62% is for the top 50 tokens of repeated prompts — so prefix cache gave ~22% token cost savings on the chat path.
[01:40] Jordan: How does that translate to tokens/sec/$? That's what the exec team keeps asking.
[01:48] Evan (Redwood CSM): On our spreadsheet snapshot: baseline (no cache, no batching) tokens/sec/$ was ~4.2k tokens per dollar for the hosted model variant. With the caching profile and 50ms batching window we hit ~6.8k tokens/$ — about 62% improvement.
[02:08] Samir (ML Eng): That seems optimistic. Was that using int8 quantization or fp16?
[02:16] Maya: Good question — those numbers are for int8 quantized runner, fp16 baseline was closer to 3.9k tokens/$. Int4 looked great in throughput (8.9k tokens/$) but we saw occasional decoding artifacts on multi-turn summarization tests.
[02:36] Holly (Product): By decoding artifacts you mean hallucinated repeats or truncated answers?
[02:42] Maya: Mostly repetition and some tokenization weirdness on structured lists — we flagged it in the evals but not catastrophic for short chat. For regulatory summarization we wouldn't ship int4 without additional eval gating.
[02:58] Alex: Okay. On latency — we need 95th < 450ms for our SLAs. How did batching affect tail latency?
[03:07] Maya: With a 50ms batching window our median latency was 120ms, 95th spiked to 610ms in bursty periods. If we reduce window to 12ms median drops slightly but 95th is ~420ms, tokens/$ decreases though (down to ~5.1k). So it's a tradeoff.
[03:29] Priya: Is the spike mostly queuing on the GPU or on network retries?
[03:34] Maya: Predominantly queueing — the roofline shows GPU utilization hitting short peaks and queuing builds on high-concurrency bursts. We can mitigate with adaptive burst lanes or reserved burst capacity on Dedicated.
[03:50] Jordan: Dedicated vs hosted — remind us the cost math for Dedicated at current pilot scale?
[03:56] Evan: At the pilot's commit tier we'd see lower per-token cost if we can hit sustained utilization above ~58%. But there's a fixed monthly fee; breakeven is about 3 months at projected usage. Dedicated also simplifies predictable 95th latency since you control capacity and preemption.
[04:15] Samir: For our traffic pattern (spiky mornings, idle nights) autoscale on Dedicated looks useful but worried about cold starts for models with big KV caches.
[04:26] Maya: We have fast warm-start snapshots for the KV — warm restore is under 4s for the current model and cache sizes, but cold boot with model load is longer. That's where prefix caching and session stickiness help.
[04:40] Alex: Security/compliance quick check — are audit logs and KMS integrated in the pilot? Procurement asked for SAML and HSM keys.
[04:48] Jordan: Yes, the private pilot profile includes KMS integration for encryption at rest and SAML SSO via our enterprise console. HSM-backed keys are supported but require Enterprise package. We'll send the exact doc.
[04:58] Holly: Please include retention windows for logs and the SOC 2 scoping.
[05:03] Evan: Will do — we have a Security pack PDF and a SOC 2 summary.
[05:09] Maya: Back to cost — we also tried variable batching per route: chat route uses 12ms window, summarization uses 50ms to accumulate tokens and push tokens/$. That hybrid improved overall econ by 18% compared to uniform 12ms.
[05:27] Priya: Can you share the per-route config? We need to feed that into our router.
[05:31] Jordan: We'll share the per-route YAML and the recommended autoscale thresholds.
[05:35] Samir: About caching: we saw diminishing returns after 70% cache hit, is there recommended eviction tuning?
[05:42] Maya: Eviction tuned by LRU with weighted key size worked well. For your workload we recommend bumping prefix cache capacity by 30% and lowering TTL for ephemeral tokens to 8 hours. That should push effective hit to mid 60s.
[05:58] Alex: How does that affect memory on the Dedicated nodes?
[06:02] Maya: Adds roughly 12GB per node for the model shard configs we're using. Not trivial but manageable for the Dedicated SKU we proposed.
[06:11] Jordan: Any competitor mentions in the RFP come up?
[06:15] Alex: We had brief chats with OpenAI for hosted simplicity and with an infra vendor that runs a self-hosted runtime. Cost-wise Redwood is competitive if caching and batching behave like this.
[06:28] Maya: Note: our fallback policy can route to a smaller model for non-critical calls during peak if you want to prioritize latency over quality; that's another lever for tokens/$.
[06:38] Holly: Can we quantify quality delta between full model and fallback model for our top 10 prompts?
[06:44] Maya: We'll run a focused eval on the top 10 prompts and return a delta matrix — expected ROUGE/ROUGE-L or similarity drop estimates.
[06:53] Priya: On instrumentation, can we push more granular token-level cost to our analytics? We're using internal billing and want to map tokens to product events.
[07:01] Evan: We can expose token breakdown per request via the per-route telemetry hooks — that'll be in the updated econ sheet.
[07:07] Jordan: Let's capture next steps then.
[07:10] Alex: Quick question — you mentioned int4 artifacts, is there a hybrid quant path? Like int8 for summarization, int4 for short chat?
[07:18] Maya: Yes, route-aware quantization is supported — the runtime will select variant by route. You can set quality gate thresholds per route so summarization keeps int8, chat can go int4.
[07:29] Samir: We'll need gating in CI for each release.
[07:33] Holly: Also please mock up a high-level runbook for an incident where cache hit drops suddenly.
[07:38] Evan: We'll add a runbook item: detect sudden cache hit drop >15% in 5m, auto-trigger rolling revive + fallback routing.
[07:47] Jordan: Great. Any final comments?
[07:50] Priya: We want the 24-hour run to include realistic user stickiness and peak concurrency at 11:00–13:00 local.
[07:57] Maya: We'll run that starting Friday at 00:00 UTC with the hybrid batching and pinned prefix cache.
[08:04] Jordan: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and action items.
[08:10] [crosstalk] Holly: Thanks!
[08:12] [END]
